entries.proposition: The exon-1 missense allele's pathogenicity rests on absence from gnomAD and in-silico scores only; no RNA, protein or functional assay of this allele alone is reported.
entries.snippet: which was absent in gnomAD with in silico prediction scores in favor of its pathogenicity

entries.proposition: The second allele is a complex structural variant: two intronic deletions (introns 4 and 5) with an inversion of exon 5.
entries.snippet: GS identified the second event, which consisted of a complex rearrangement with two intronic deletions (introns 4 and 5) associated with an inversion of exon 5

entries.proposition: RNA consequence was measured in blood by RT-PCR across exons 4-6: a 186 bp product appears beside the expected 293 bp product.
entries.snippet: using primers encompassing exons 4 through 6, obtained from blood, revealed the presence of a shorter amplicon isoform (186 bp) in addition to the expected 293 bp band

entries.proposition: Amplicon sequencing attributes the 186 bp product to exon 5 skipping caused by the structural variant, i.e. the measured RNA consequence belongs to the SV allele, not to the missense allele.
entries.snippet: Amplicon-sequencing analysis of the 186 bp gel-purified PCR product demonstrated that the structural variant caused exon 5 skipping

entries.proposition: The authors themselves state that blood and fibroblasts may be inadequate to model genes expressed mainly in the central nervous system.
entries.snippet: Clinically accessible tissues such as blood samples, skin and muscle biopsies, as well as cell cultures (e.g., Epstein–Barr-transformed lymphocytes, fibroblast cell lines) are sometimes inadequate to model genes prevalently expressed in the central nervous system
